title: A neutral coupled periodic orbit excludes energy-only harmonic-electric integrability

periodic_orbit.model: Use the spatially homogeneous torus sector of Maxwell--Klein--Gordon with two equal-mass complex scalars phi_+ and phi_- of charges +e and -e, temporal gauge, and the symmetric half-normalized matter Lagrangian. The reduced equations are phi_sigma''+(m^2+e^2|a|^2)phi_sigma=0 and a''+e^2(|phi_+|^2+|phi_-|^2)a=0, with Gauss density e Im(conj(phi_+)phi_+')-e Im(conj(phi_-)phi_-').
periodic_orbit.exact_solution: For A,R>0 set Omega=sqrt(2)eR, omega=sqrt(m^2+e^2A^2), a(t)=A(cos(Omega t),sin(Omega t),0), and phi_+(t)=phi_-(t)=R exp(i omega t). Then |a| and both scalar amplitudes are constant, and the displayed equations hold exactly.
periodic_orbit.gauss_neutrality: The two scalar phases are identical while their charges are opposite, so their Gauss densities cancel pointwise. The spatial currents add and provide the centripetal Maxwell current required by a''=-2e^2R^2 a.
periodic_orbit.nonintegrable_harmonic_electric: The harmonic electric field is E_bar=-a' and has constant magnitude A Omega>0. Thus int_0^T |E_bar(t)|dt=A Omega T and the holonomy total variation diverges linearly although the exact reduced Hamiltonian is constant and finite.
periodic_orbit.obstruction: Positive conserved energy plus Gauss neutrality and the coupled Maxwell current structure do not imply the L1_t harmonic-electric hypothesis used in K1584. A global radius proof must use additional dispersion, exclusion of the homogeneous charged sector, damping/scattering, or a cancellation/normal form that does not spend total variation.
periodic_orbit.scope_guard: This is a two-species charge-neutral counterexample to an energy-only generic implication. It does not prove failure for every one-species constrained model, exclude dispersive small-data results, or disprove a cancellation-based positive-radius theorem.
